text:
Maria G.: Quick update from the weekend perf runs — did an apples-to-apples comparison (replay harness) for kernel-selector v2 vs v1. Short summary: v2 improves p50 by ~18% and p95 by ~9% on typical short-chat loads, but we see a regression on long-tail long-sequence tails when batch_size > 8.

Sam K.: nice. can you paste the exact harness command + config?

Maria G.: sure — replay harness used recorded-prod-traces (~120k requests), synthetic ramp to 500qps peak, 60m run. command:```./replay_runner --trace-dir=prod_traces/2026-03 --concurrency=64 --target-qps=500 --workload=chat_short+long_tail --kernel-selector=v2 --batcher=stride-v3 --kv-mode=dynamic```

Maria G.: config snippet we toggled:```kernel_selector: v2  # heuristics: prefer matmul-fused for len<128, aten-nt for >512
batcher:
  type: stride-v3
  max_batch: 32
  latency_slo_ms: 150
kv_cache:
  mode: dynamic
  hot_prefix_ttl_s: 120
  eviction: lru_weighted
quant_profiles:
  default: q8_legacy
  aggressive: q4_68```

perf-bot: Summary: v2 vs v1 (short-chat workload): p50 18% lower, p95 9% lower, throughput +12%. Long-tail workload (>=2048 tokens) with batch_size>=8: p95 +20% (regression). See attached perf table in logs. :bar_chart:

Raj P.: I dug into traces — the long-tail regression seems KV cache churn + kernel-selector fallback. For long sequences many requests push KV beyond per-GPU cache budget triggering LRU eviction; kernel-selector then switches to aten-nt (safer but slower) mid-request for subsequent chunks. That causes tail latency spikes.

Eva L.: did you try pinning hot prefixes or sticky routing to reduce eviction?

Raj P.: yes. experiment: set hot_prefix_ttl_s=600 and turned on "sticky-kv": true for sessions with prefix hit rate >0.7. Result: long-tail p95 improved by ~11% vs earlier v2 run, but short-chat p50 increases slightly (~3%) because sticky routing reduces batching efficiency.

Kyle T.: tradeoffs expected. any numbers on quantization + speculative decoding?

Maria G.: ran three Q experiments on the same replay set: q8 baseline, q4 agressive, q4 + speculative(lookahead=2). Results: q4 alone drops p95 a bit (faster) but we measured a small quality drop on the eval set (conv-turn-level BLEU-ish metrics down ~0.6%). q4 + speculative recovered ~60% of latency gains while keeping quality within 0.2% of baseline.

Maria G.: short table from the run logs (excerpt):```workload | kernel | quant | spec | p50_ms | p95_ms | quality_delta
short    | v2     | q8    | no   | 28     | 132    | 0.0%
short    | v2     | q4    | no   | 22     | 118    | -0.6%
short    | v2     | q4    | yes  | 20     | 110    | -0.2%
longtail | v2     | q8    | no   | 160    | 420    | 0.0%
longtail | v2     | q4    | no   | 140    | 500    | -1.2%  # more regression due to kernel fallbacks
longtail | v2     | q4    | yes  | 135    | 340    | -0.9%```

Sam K.: interesting that q4 made longtail worse in p95 — is that because of numerical instability forcing kernel fallback?

Raj P.: exactly. lower-precision kernels sometimes fail fast or have slower spill paths; kernel-selector detects mismatch and falls back to safe kernels, but that fallback happens mid-generation causing huge tail spikes. We need better detection/windowing in selector so it doesn't flip kernels frequently inside a request.

Eva L.: sounds like two orthogonal fixes: 1) make kernel-selector sticky per-request with a probation window (e.g., don't switch unless sustained metric >5 chunks), 2) improve KV eviction heuristics (pin hot prefixes or quota by session).

Maria G.: proposed changes we want to test next: - kernel-selector: add per-request sticky_mode + switch_threshold=3 chunks - batcher: adaptive max_batch that lowers for long-seq heavy workers - kv-cache: session_quota 50MB + hot_prefix_ttl_s=600 - regression_gate: block canary/promote if p95 increases >5% for any top-10 workload measured on replay harness

Kyle T.: I can put up a perf/regression gate PR. For gating, do we use absolute ms or relative %? I'd vote relative % for cross-model fairness.

Maria G.: relative % w/ floor: block if rel increase >5% AND absolute increase >10ms for that workload. prevents noisy tiny baselines.

perf-bot: Action items created: PF-314 (sticky kernel selector), PF-315 (kv session quotas), PF-316 (adaptive batcher), PF-317 (regression gate). Links: https://redwood/slack-links/PF-314 etc.

Sam K.: final question — are synthetic-only runs misleading? I saw some teams using only synthetic Gaussian arrivals; our replay harness caught cache & seq-distribution effects others missed.

Maria G.: yes — synthetic ramps are fine for baseline throughput. But apples-to-apples requires replay of real request shapes and seq-lens; synthetic doesn't capture prefix locality or multi-request sessions that drive KV hits. Always include at least one replay run for regression gates.

Raj P.: bonus note: profiling traces show kernel-selector decision overhead is tiny (~0.4ms avg), so stickiness won't add overhead. Biggest slowdowns are eviction stalls (hundreds ms when cold).

Eva L.: ok i'm writing the eval checklist for the gate (will include quality thresholds + replay harness command + diff commands).

Maria G.: thanks all — next step: run v2 + sticky + kv-session-quota + q4+spec for 3 runs and post consolidated CSV. I'll follow up in this thread. :thumbsup:

Kyle T.: grabbing PF-317 to implement gating logic.

Maria G.: last note: keep an eye for p99 outliers in logs — those correlate with cross-GPU cache-sync events. we'll instrument more counters on the next run.
